ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.claim: The successful are content with God's will through prosperity and hardship, fulfilling others' rights when favoured and remaining patient when tried.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.anchor: they showed patience and resolve and expressed contentment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r2.claim: The peaceful soul is the opposite of those who respond to ease with pride and hardship with despair; it stays true in both, gives thanks and helps others in ease, and perseveres in adversity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r2.anchor: If they are blessed with favours, they think that they are being tested whether they show gratitude to the Almighty or not

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r3.claim: Those content with God through comfort and adversity are called contented souls and will dwell in Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r3.anchor: These are the people who will dwell in Paradise.

QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r16.claim: The tranquil soul may be the spirit settled toward the still soul, or a soul made tranquil by gnosis, remembrance of God, or glad tidings of Paradise.
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r16.anchor: المطمئنة بالمعرفة : ويقال : المطمئنة بذكر الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is secure from fear and grief or settled in truth without doubt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r1.anchor: الآمنة التي لا يلحقها خوف ولا حزن، أو التي كانت مطمئنة إلى الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the address comes at death as the believer's soul leaves the body; others place it at resurrection or entry into Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد: يقال لها ذلك عند الموت وخروجها من جسد المؤمن

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:24-27/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:24-27/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:24-27/r4.claim: The tranquil soul rests through remembrance of God, ascending causes to the Necessary Being and finding sufficiency in knowing Him, or is secure from fear and grief; readings express both senses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:24-27/r4.anchor: { يأيتها النفس المطمئنة } على إرادة القول وهي التي اطمأنت بذكر الله

BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.claim: The natural contrasts prepare for testing through wealth or deprivation and the opposed outcomes of tyrants and the tranquil soul.
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.anchor: أو بالفقر والحرمان، وما يظن معهما من إكرام أو إهانة، ثم التقابل في المصير ما بين عذاب الطاغين المغرورين، ونعيم النفس المطمئنة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r6.claim: The tranquil soul is settled, steadfast, and oriented toward truth; it is addressed at death and again at resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r6.anchor: فأما النفس الزكية المطمئنة وهي الساكنة الثابتة الدائرة مع الحق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r9.claim: A report through al-Dahhak says the tranquil-soul verse was revealed concerning Uthman ibn Affan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس: نزلت في عثمان بن عفان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r10.speaker: بريدة بن الحصيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r10.claim: Buraidah ibn al-Husayb says the verse was revealed about Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r10.anchor: وعن بريدة بن الحصيب: نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب، رضي الله عنه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r11.claim: Al-Awfi's report from Ibn Abbas says the address on Judgment Day calls each soul back to its body, its companion in worldly life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r11.anchor: يعني: صاحبك، وهو بدنها الذي كانت تعمره في الدنيا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p401/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p401/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p401/r1.claim: The Prophet taught a supplication asking God for a tranquil soul that believes in meeting Him, accepts His decree, and is content with His provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p401/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لرجل: "قل اللهم، إني أسألك نفسا بك مطمئنة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p401/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p401/r2.speaker: أبو سليمان بن زبر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p401/r2.claim: Abu Sulayman ibn Zabr says the report of Rawahah is her sole transmitted hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p401/r2.anchor: عن أبي سليمان بن زبر أنه قال: حديث رواحة هذا واحد أمه.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r7.claim: The tranquil soul means the believer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r7.anchor: أحدها : يعني المؤمنة , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r8.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r8.claim: It may mean the responsive soul.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r9.claim: It may mean the soul that believes what God has promised.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r9.anchor: الثالث : المؤمنة بما وعد الله , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r10.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r10.claim: Ubayy's reading says the secure, tranquil soul.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r10.anchor: وهو في حرف أبي بن كعب يا أيتها النفس الآمنة المطمئنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r11.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r11.claim: It may mean the satisfied soul.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r12.speaker: أصحاب الخواطر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r12.claim: Some spiritual interpreters say the soul is tranquil in worldly life and is called to return by leaving it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r12.anchor: السادس : ما قاله بعض أصحاب الخواطر : المطمئنة إلى الدنيا , ارجعي إلى ربك في تركها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r13.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r13.claim: When God intends to take a believer's soul, it becomes tranquil toward God and God is pleased with it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r13.anchor: ما قاله الحسن أن الله تعالى إذا أراد أن يقبض روح عبده المؤمن اطمأنت النفس إلى الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r25.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r25.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr, who admired it while sitting with the Prophet; the Prophet told him that people would say this to him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r25.anchor: نزلت في أبي بكر , فروى ابن عباس أنها نزلت وأبو بكر جالس فقال : يا رسول الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r26.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r26.claim: Another report says it was revealed about Uthman when he endowed the well of Ruma.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r26.anchor: الثاني : أنها نزلت في عثمان حين وقف بئر رومة , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r27.speaker: بريدة الأسلمي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r27.claim: Another report says it was revealed about Hamza.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r27.anchor: الثالث : أنها نزلت في حمزة , قاله بريدة الأسلمي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r28.speaker: عكرمة والفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r28.claim: Alternatively, the verse applies generally to all believers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r28.anchor: الرابع : أنها عامة في كل المؤمنين , رواه عكرمة والفراء .

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Later additions in 23–24 and 27–30 bring the afterlife dimension into the sura and help decode the enigmatic oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: Spätere Zusätze (V. 23.24 und V. 27–30) tragen diese eschatologische Dimension dann auch in die vorliegende Sure ein

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.claim: Verses 23–24 and 27–30 are later insertions that expand the original four-verse eschatological unit and enact the oath's duality as an antithesis.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 23.24 sind wie V. 27–30 spätere Einschübe (s. o.), die das eschatologische Vierergesätz

TABATABAI:89:23-28/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r6.claim: The tranquil soul rests in God, accepts His choices, knows itself to be God's servant, and sees worldly gain and loss as a test; it neither grows arrogant through blessings nor ungrateful in poverty.
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r6.anchor: هي التي تسكن إلى ربها وترضى بما رضي به فترى نفسها عبدا لا يملك لنفسه شيئا

TABATABAI:89:23-28/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r7.claim: Such a soul remains in steady servitude, avoiding excess and neglect, unlike the worldly and rebellious person described earlier.
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r7.anchor: بل هو في مستقر من العبودية لا ينحرف عن مستقيم صراطه بإفراط أو تفريط

THALABI:v10p202/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p202/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p202/r8.claim: The reassured soul is one that trusts what God has promised and affirms what He has said.
THALABI:v10p202/r8.anchor: يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة إلى ما وعد الله المصدقة بما قال

THALABI:v10p202/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p202/r9.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p202/r9.claim: He describes the soul as repentant and humble, certain that God is its Lord and resolute in obeying Him.
THALABI:v10p202/r9.anchor: مجاهد: المنيبة المخبتة التي قد أيقنت أن الله سبحانه ربنا

THALABI:v10p202/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p202/r10.speaker: المسييب عن الكلبي وأبي روق
THALABI:v10p202/r10.claim: They say the soul becomes reassured when God brightens its face and gives it its record in its right hand.
THALABI:v10p202/r10.anchor: المسييب: سمعت الكلبي وأبا روق يقولان: هي التي يبيض الله وجهها ويعطيها كتابها بيمينها

THALABI:v10p202/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p202/r11.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p202/r11.claim: He calls it the believing and certain soul.

THALABI:v10p202/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p202/r12.speaker: عطية
THALABI:v10p202/r12.claim: He says it is content with God's decree.

THALABI:v10p202/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p202/r13.speaker: حيان عن الكلبي
THALABI:v10p202/r13.claim: He describes it as safe from God's punishment.
THALABI:v10p202/r13.anchor: حيان عن الكلبي: الآمنة من عذاب الله تعالى

THALABI:v10p202/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p202/r14.speaker: أبي
THALABI:v10p202/r14.claim: His reading adds the adjective 'safe' before 'reassured'.
THALABI:v10p202/r14.anchor: في قراءة أبي يا أيتها النفس الآمنة المطمئنة

THALABI:v10p203/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p203/r1.claim: He describes the soul as content with God's decree, knowing that what reaches it could not have missed it and what misses it could not have reached it.
THALABI:v10p203/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة قال: الراضية بقضاء الله التي قد علمت أن ما أصابها لم يكن ليخطئها

THALABI:v10p203/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p203/r2.claim: He interprets the reassured soul as the sincere soul.

THALABI:v10p203/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
THALABI:v10p203/r3.claim: He says it is the soul that knows God and cannot bear to be apart from Him even briefly.
THALABI:v10p203/r3.anchor: ابن عطاء: هي العارفة بالله سبحانه التي لا تصبر عنه طرفة عين

THALABI:v10p203/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p203/r4.claim: Other explanations call it the soul reassured by remembrance of God, or one that trusts God and His promised provision.
THALABI:v10p203/r4.anchor: وقيل: المطمئنة بذكر الله. بيانه: وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله

THALABI:v10p203#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r2.speaker: سعيد عن النبي
THALABI:v10p203#2/r2.claim: When Abu Bakr admired the verse, the Prophet said an angel would say these words to him at death.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r2.anchor: قرأ رجل عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة قال أبو بكر: ما أحسن هذا

THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.claim: At Ibn Abbas's burial, a bird entered his coffin and was not seen leaving; the verse was recited at the grave, though its reciter was unseen.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: مات ابن عباس بالطائف فجاء طائر لم ير على خلقه

THALABI:v10p204/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r3.speaker: أهل الإشارة
THALABI:v10p204/r3.claim: They address the soul settled in worldly life and call it to leave it for God and the afterlife; it is content with God and accepted by Him.
THALABI:v10p204/r3.anchor: يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة إلى الدنيا ارجعي إلى الله بتركها والرجوع إلى الله هو سلوك سبيل الآخرة

THALABI:v10p204/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r6.speaker: ابن بريدة
THALABI:v10p204/r6.claim: He says the verse refers to Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, whose soul was honored after he was martyred at Uhud until God returns it to his body.
THALABI:v10p204/r6.anchor: عن ابن بريدة في هذه الآية يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة قال: نفس حمزة بن عبد المطلب

THALABI:v10p204/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p204/r7.claim: The verse was also said to concern Habib ibn Adi, whose face God turned toward the qibla after he prayed while crucified; its ruling applies generally to all reassured believers.
THALABI:v10p204/r7.anchor: وقد نزلت في حبيب بن عدي الذي صلبه أهل مكة وجعلوا وجهه إلى المدينة

ELMALILI:89:16-26#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#3/r1.claim: The next passage contrasts the fate of the person attached to worldly pleasures with that of the soul content with God, His remembrance, obedience, and approval.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#3/r1.anchor: Dünyaya gönül bağlayan ve itmi’nânını ancak dünya lezâizinde bulan kâfir insanın âkıbeti bu olduğu anlatıldıktan sonra

QASHANI:89:27-30/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:27-30/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:27-30/r1.claim: The tranquil soul has received serenity and been illuminated by certainty, becoming at rest in God instead of agitation.
QASHANI:89:27-30/r1.anchor: التي نزلت عليها السكينة وتنورت بنور اليقين فاطمأنت إلى الله من الاضطراب

SULAMI:v2p394#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is a spirit joined to the Real, content with His decree, and summoned to return to the One who adorned it and readied it for return.
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r1.anchor: قال القاسم في هذه الآية : ﴿ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ﴾

SULAMI:v2p394#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r2.claim: God clothes the tranquil soul in guidance until it becomes a self-reproaching soul.
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r2.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله : النفس المطمئنة ألبسها الحق اوصاف الهداية

SULAMI:v2p394#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r3.claim: The soul is content with worldly life but must return to God by leaving it and taking the path of the afterlife.
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم في قوله : ﴿ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ﴾ ، إلى الدنيا

SULAMI:v2p394#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r4.claim: The tranquil soul is a knower of God who cannot endure separation from Him even for an instant.
SULAMI:v2p394#4/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : المطمئنة هي العارفة بالله التي لا تصبر عن الله طرفة عين

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r1.claim: When Abu Bakr admired the verse, the Prophet told him that these words would be said to him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية قال : نزلت وابو بكر جالس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r2.claim: A second report places Abu Bakr reading the verses to the Prophet, who says an angel will say this to him at death.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : قرات عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r3.claim: A report about Uthman purchasing the well of Rumah to provide public water says God then revealed the tranquil soul verse concerning him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : من يشتري بئر رومة نستعذب بها غفر الله له

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r4.speaker: بريدة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r4.claim: Buraida says the tranquil soul is Hamza.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r4.anchor: عن بريدة رضي الله عنه في قوله : يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة قال : يعني نفس حمزة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r5.claim: Mujahid says the tranquil soul is one certain that God is its Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله : يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة قال التي ايقنت بان الله ربها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says that when God takes a believer, the soul and God are mutually pleased; He then takes it into Paradise among His righteous servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة الاية قال : ان الله اذا اراد قبض عبده المؤمن اطمانت النفس اليه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.claim: Qatada says the tranquil soul is a believer reassured by God's promise and that entering among His servants means joining the righteous.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.anchor: عن قتادة يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة قال : هذا المؤمن اطمان إلى ما وعد الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the soul receives the good news of Paradise at death, resurrection, and the gathering.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم رضي الله عنه يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة الاية قال : بشرت بالجنة عند الموت وعند البعث ويوم الجمع

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that after Ibn Abbas died at Taif, an unseen bird entered his bier and did not emerge; the tranquil-soul verses were heard recited at his grave.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : مات ابن عباس بالطائف ، فجاء طير لم ير على خلقه ، فدخل نعشه ثم لم ير خارجا منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p335/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p335/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p335/r1.claim: The passage turns from threats of worldly punishment to unavoidable punishment in the next life, when compelled remembrance and regret will be useless.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p335/r1.anchor: انتقل به من تهديدهم بعذاب الدنيا الذي في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p335/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p335/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p335/r2.claim: The preceding description of the earth's crushing and Hell is staging that builds suspense and magnifies the Day; the chief messages are the severe torment and the address to the reassured soul.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p335/r2.anchor: فهو توطئة وتشويق لسماع ما يجيء بعده وتهويل لشأن ذلك اليوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.claim: The passage ends the warnings with glad tidings for believers guided by the Quran, following the Quran's pattern of joining promise to warning to encourage good and deter evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.anchor: ختم الكلام بالبشارة للمؤمنين الذين تذكروا بالقرآن واتبعوا هديه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.claim: Alternatively, the address may begin a new passage, prompted by the mention of punishment for the polytheist, and God may be speaking directly to the believers' reassured souls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الآية استئنافا ابتدائيا جرى على مناسبة ذكر عذاب الإنسان المشرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the verse was revealed concerning ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān after he donated the well of Rumah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r4.anchor: فعن الضحاك : أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان لما تصدق ببئر رومة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r5.speaker: بريدة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r5.claim: Buraydah says the verse was revealed about Ḥamzah after his death as a martyr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r5.anchor: وعن بريدة : أنها نزلت في حمزة حين قتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r6.claim: Another reported view applies the verse to Khubayb ibn ʿAdī when the Meccans crucified him; these specific occasions imply a Medinan revelation, against the agreed Meccan classification except for a report from al-Dānī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r6.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في خبيب بن عدي لما صلبه أهل مكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r7.claim: If the verse is Medinan, it is separate from the preceding passage and was placed here by instruction or revealed afterward because of thematic affinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r7.anchor: وهي على هذا منفصلة عما قبلها كتبت هنا بتوقيف خاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن حارثة وأبي بن كعب وابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r8.claim: These authorities say the words are spoken at resurrection as spirits return to bodies; on this view the passage connects to the earth being crushed, and the return is literal, with the body as the soul's Lord or owner.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وزيد بن حارثة وأبي بن كعب وابنن مسعود : أن هذا يقال عند البعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r9.speaker: زيد بن حارثة وأبو صالح
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Ḥārithah and Abū Ṣāliḥ say the address is given to the soul at death; Zayd specifically says the believer's soul is thereby promised Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r9.anchor: وعن زيد بن حارثة وأبي صالح : يقال هذا للنفس عند الموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that after a man recited the verse before the Prophet and Abū Bakr praised it, the Prophet said an angel would say it to Abū Bakr at death; no grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r10.anchor: وقد روى الطبري عن سعيد بن جبير قال : قرأ رجل عند رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r11.claim: Nafs can mean the whole person, as in two cited verses, or the spirit that gives bodily life, as in another.

TUSTARI:89:27/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:27/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:27/r1.claim: The address is to the spirit-soul that gives life to the natural soul; the reassured soul believes in God's reward and punishment.
TUSTARI:89:27/r1.anchor: هذا خطاب لنفس الروح الذي به حياة نفس الطبع والمطمئنة المصدقة بثواب الله وعقابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r3.claim: The tranquil soul is one possessing complete certainty, a degree beyond faith in which no question remains to be resolved.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r3.anchor: والمطمئنة معناه: الموقنة غاية اليقين، ألا ترى أن إبراهيم عليه السلام قال: ولكن ليطمئن قلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة وبريدة الأسلمي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r1.claim: One view says the verse was revealed about Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib after his martyrdom at Uḥud, according to Abū Hurayra and Burayda al-Aslamī.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r1.anchor: أحدها في حمزة بن عبد المطلب لما استشهد يوم أحد قاله أبو هريرة وبريدة الأسلمي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it was revealed about ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān when he endowed the Rūma well.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r2.anchor: والثاني في عثمان بن عفان حين أوقف بئر رومة قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r3.claim: Muqātil says it was revealed about Khubayb ibn ʿAdī when Meccans crucified him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r3.anchor: والثالث في خبيب بن عدي لما صلبه أهل مكة قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī transmits the view that the verse was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r4.anchor: والرابع في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says it addresses all believers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r5.anchor: والخامس [ في ] جميع المؤمنين قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r6.claim: One meaning of muṭmaʾinna is believer; al-Zajjāj glosses it as secure in faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r6.anchor: أحدها المؤمنة قاله ابن عباس وقال الزجاج المطمئنة بالإيمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r7.claim: Mujāhid says the soul is content with God's decree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r7.anchor: والثاني الراضية بقضاء الله قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r8.claim: Qatāda says the soul is certain of what God promised.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r8.anchor: والثالث الموقنة بما وعد الله قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r9.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r9.claim: Most say the soul is addressed as it leaves worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r9.anchor: أحدهما عند خروجها من الدنيا قاله الأكثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r10.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r10.claim: Another view says it is addressed at resurrection, when God orders souls to return to their bodies.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p123/r10.anchor: والثاني عند البعث يقال لها ارجعي إلى صاحبك والى جسدك

FARRA:v3p262/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p262/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p262/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is secure in faith and affirms the reward and resurrection.
FARRA:v3p262/r1.anchor:
وقوله عز وجل: «يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة (27) .
بالإيمان والمصدقة بالثواب والبعث

JISHUMI:v10p7409/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r8.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r8.claim: Ubayy’s codex is reported to read “the secure, obedient soul”; another has “among My servant,” and both variants are treated as explanatory readings.
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r8.anchor: وروي أن في مصحف أبي: (النفس الآمنة المطيعة)، وعن بعضهم (في عبدي)

JISHUMI:v10p7410/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r6.claim: One report says the “tranquil soul” was revealed about Ḥamza b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib after his martyrdom at Uḥud.
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r6.anchor: وقيل: نزل قوله: (ياأيتها النفس المطمئنة) في حمزة بن عبد المطلب حين استشهد يوم أحد

JISHUMI:v10p7410/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r7.claim: Another report concerns Khubayb b. ʿAdī, who prayed that God turn his face to the qibla if he had good with Him; God turned it, and no one could turn it back.
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r7.anchor: وقيل: نزل في خبيب بن عدي لما قتله أهل مكة

JISHUMI:v10p7410/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r8.claim: Another view applies the verse generally to all believers.
JISHUMI:v10p7410/r8.anchor: وقيل: بل الآية عامة في جميع المؤمنين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r1.claim: The address is an implied divine saying to the believer, spoken directly in honor as with Moses or through an angel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r1.anchor: على إرادة القول ، أي : يقول الله للمؤمن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r2.claim: The tranquil soul is secure from fear and grief, or a believing soul settled in truth by certainty; Ubayy's reading supports the first sense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r2.anchor: المطمئنة } الآمنة التي لا يستفزها خوف ولا حزن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r3.claim: The address may come at death, resurrection, or entry into Paradise, meaning return to the reward promised by the Lord.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r3.anchor: إما عند الموت . وإما عند البعث ، وإما عند دخول الجنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r9.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r9.claim: Ubayy reads the address as coming to the Lord content and approved, then entering into God's servant.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبي : ( ائتي ربك راضية مرضية ، ادخلي في عبدي )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r10.claim: Specific occasions are reported about Hamza and Khubayb ibn Adi, but the author says the apparent reading is general.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r10.anchor: فحول الله وجهه نحوها فلم يستطع أحد أن يحوله ، والظاهر العموم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r11.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting al-Fajr during the ten nights and light on Judgment Day for reciting it at other times.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r11.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1301 ) ( من قرأ سورة الفجر

MUJAHID:v2p757#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p757#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p757#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the tranquil soul is humble and at peace with its Lord.
MUJAHID:v2p757#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ﴾ يعني المخبتة المطمئنة إلى ربها

MUQATIL:89:27-30/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is one reassured by faith.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339/r1.claim: God addresses the soul to honor it, as He addressed Moses, or an angel speaks on God's behalf; the tranquil soul is secure from fear and grief or settled in certainty.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339/r1.anchor: ﴿ يا أيتها النفس ﴾ اكراما له كما كلم موسى عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339/r2.claim: Abu's reading “O secure and tranquil soul” supports the first interpretation; the address may occur at death, resurrection, or entry into Paradise.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339/r2.anchor: قراءة أبى يا أيتها النفس الآمنة

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r1.claim: The passage contrasts the worldly-minded person who accuses God over wealth and poverty with the soul trusting and submitting to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r1.anchor: لما ذكر حال من كانت همته الدنيا فاتهم الله في إغنائه وإفقاره، ذكر حال من اطمأنت نفسه إلى الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r2.claim: It is also said that the address comes from angels to God’s friends.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول الملائكة لأولياء الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r3.claim: Mujahid and others define the tranquil soul as certain that God is its Lord and humbly submits to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r3.anchor: النفس المطمئنة: الساكنة الموقنة أيقنت أن الله ربها، فأخبتت لذلك قاله مجاهد وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the soul is assured of God’s reward; he also glosses it as the believer.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أي المطمئنة بثواب الله. وعنه المؤمنة

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r5.claim: Al-Hasan defines it as the believing soul that is certain.

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r6.claim: Mujahid also describes the soul as content with God’s decree, knowing what misses it could not have reached it and vice versa.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r6.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا: الراضية بقضاء الله، التي علمت أن ما أخطأها لم يكن ليصيبها

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r7.claim: Muqatil says the soul is safe from God’s punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الآمنة من عذاب الله

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r8.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r8.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab’s reading adds “secure” before “tranquil.”
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r8.anchor: وفي حرف أبي بن كعب «يأيتها النفس الآمنة المطمئنة»

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r9.claim: One view describes a soul acting in certainty of what God promised in His Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r9.anchor: وقيل: التي عملت على يقين بما وعد الله في كتابه

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r10.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r10.claim: Ibn Kaysan glosses the tranquil soul as sincere.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r10.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: المطمئنة هنا: المخلصة

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r11.speaker: ابن عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r11.claim: Ibn Ata calls it the knowing soul that cannot bear separation from God for a moment.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء: العارفة التي لا تصبر عنه طرفة عين

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r12.claim: Another view links tranquility to remembrance of God, supported by 13:28.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r12.anchor: وقيل: المطمئنة بذكر الله تعالى بيانه الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r13.claim: Another view says the soul is tranquil through faith and belief in resurrection and reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r13.anchor: وقيل: المطمئنة بالإيمان، المصدقة بالمبعث والثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says she is tranquil because she receives glad tidings of Paradise at death, resurrection, and the gathering.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r14.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: المطمئنة لأنها بشرت بالجنة عند الموت، وعند البعث، ويوم الجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r15.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r15.claim: Abdullah ibn Burayda transmits from his father that the verse means Hamza’s soul.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r15.anchor: وروى عبد الله بن بريدة عن أبيه قال: يعني نفس حمزة

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r16.claim: Al-Qurtubi’s preferred scope is general: every sincere, obedient believer.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r16.anchor: والصحيح أنها عامة في كل نفس مؤمن مخلص طائع

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r17.speaker: الحسن البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r17.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says that as God takes a believer’s soul, it is tranquil with God and God is tranquil with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r17.anchor: قال الحسن البصري: إن الله تعالى إذا أراد أن يقبض روح عبده المؤمن، اطمأنت النفس إلى الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r18.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r18.claim: Amr ibn al-As describes two angels bringing a gift from Paradise and calling the soul content and pleasing; it leaves like the finest musk scent.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r18.anchor: وقال عمرو بن العاص: إذا توفي المؤمن أرسل الله إليه ملكين، وأرسل معهما تحفة من الجنة، فيقولان لها: اخرجي أيتها النفس المطمئنة راضية مرضية

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r19.speaker: سعيد بن زايد
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r19.claim: Said ibn Zayd reports that after a man recited the verse, the Prophet told Abu Bakr an angel would say it to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27/r19.anchor:
وقال سعيد بن زايد:
" قرأ رجل عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r1.claim: Said ibn Jubayr reports that a strange bird entered Ibn Abbas’s coffin at his death in Taif and was never seen leaving; the verse was recited at his grave by an unknown reciter.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r1.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: مات ابن عباس بالطائف، فجاء طائر لم ير على خلقته طائر قط، فدخل نعشه

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r2.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan when he endowed the well of Rumah.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r2.anchor: وروى الضحاك: أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه حين وقف بئر رومة

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r3.claim: Another report says it was revealed about Khubayb ibn Adi, crucified by Meccans, whose face God turned toward the qibla.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r3.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في خبيب بن عدي الذي صلبه أهل مكة، وجعلوا وجهه إلى المدينة، فحول الله وجهه نحو القبلة

NAHHAS:v5p225/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p225/r1.claim: Al-nafs is an adjective of ayyu, and al-muṭmaʾinnah modifies al-nafs; if it modifies ayyu instead, it may be accusative after the clause is complete.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r1.anchor: ويجوز يا أيها لإبهام أي النفس نعت لأي والمطمئنة نعت للنفس

NAHHAS:v5p225/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p225/r2.claim: The tranquil soul is reassured by God's promise and warning.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r2.anchor: والمعنى المطمئنة بوعد الله جل وعز ووعيده

QUTB-ZILAL:89:27/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:27/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:27/r1.claim: In the midst of terror and punishment, the believing soul is called from the highest assembly in an intimate, honoring, reassuring address.

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r1.claim: Razi contrasts a soul settled in worldly life with one settled in knowledge of God and worship.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r1.anchor: لما وصف حال من اطمأن إلى الدنيا ، وصف حال من أطمأن إلى معرفته وعبوديته

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r2.claim: The divine address may be spoken directly to the believer, as God spoke to Moses, or delivered by an angel.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r2.anchor: فإما أن يكلمه إكراما له كما كلم موسى عليه السلام أو على لسان ملك

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r3.claim: Al-Qaffāl says the command functions as a statement: a tranquil soul returns to God; imperative wording can carry declarative force.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r3.anchor: هذا وإن كان أمرا في الظاهر لكنه خبر في المعنى ، والتقدير أن النفس إذا كانت مطمئنة رجعت إلى الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r4.claim: Iṭmiʾnān means settledness and firmness; one explanation is certainty in truth without doubt, as in 2:260.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r4.anchor: هذا الاستقرار وجوه أحدها : أن تكون متيقنة بالحق ، فلا يخالجها شك

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r5.claim: A reading by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb adds “secure,” describing the soul as free of fear and grief.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r5.anchor: ويشهد لهذا التفسير قراءة أبي بن كعب يا أيتها النفس الآمنة المطمئنة

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r6.claim: This security may arise at death upon hearing the promise in 41:30, at resurrection, and certainly upon entering Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r6.anchor: وتحصل عند البعث ، وعند دخول الجنة لا محالة

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r7.claim: Razi argues from Qur'an and reason that true tranquility comes only through remembrance of God, as 13:28 states.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r7.anchor: القرآن والبرهان تطابقا على أن هذا الاطمئنان لا يحصل إلا بذكر الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r8.claim: Reason ascends through contingent causes until it reaches the Necessary Existent, where its search and need stop.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r8.anchor: حتى ينتهي في ذلك الترقي إلى واجب الوجود لذاته مقطع الحاجات

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r9.claim: Finite things cannot meet unlimited needs; stability requires God's inexhaustible perfection.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r9.anchor: فلا بد في مقابلة حاجة العبد التي لا نهاية لها من كمال الله الذي لا نهاية له

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r10.claim: The perfected soul is intimate with God, longs for Him, and speaks with Him at death, though Razi says this account requires intellectual or spiritual attainment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r10.anchor: كان أنسه بالله وشوقه إلى الله وبقاؤه بالله وكلامه مع الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r11.claim: Razi says this account is useful only to someone advanced in divine thought or spiritual detachment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r11.anchor: وهذا كلام لا ينتفع الإنسان به إلا إذا كان كاملا في القوة الفكرية الإلهية أو في التجريد والتفريد

RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r1.claim: The Qur'an describes the self as unspecific, commanding evil, self-reproaching, and tranquil, citing 91:7, 5:116, 32:17, 12:53, and 75:2.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r1.anchor: وصفها بكونها أمارة بالسوء ، فقال : { إن النفس لامارة بالسوء } ( يوسف : 53 ) وتارة بكونها

RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r2.claim: The self is the “I” that says it acted, saw, heard, desired, imagined, and remembered.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r2.anchor: وهي التي تشير إليها بقولك : ( أنا ) حين تخبر عن نفسك بقولك فعلت ورأيت وسمعت

RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r3.claim: The self cannot simply be the body: one may know the self when unaware of the body, and the known differs from what is unknown.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r3.anchor: قد يكون معلوما حال ما تكون هذه البنية المخصوصة غير معلومة ، والمعلوم غير ما هو غير معلوم

RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r4.claim: The self also persists as bodily parts change, so it is not identical to the changing bodily structure.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r4.anchor: هذه البنية متبدلة الأجزاء والمشار إليه بقولك : ( أنا ) غير متبدل

RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r5.claim: Some argue that the self is immaterial because one can apprehend “I” without noticing the body; Razi refers readers to his al-Lubāb for an objection.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r5.anchor: قال قوم إن النفس ليست بجسم لأنا قد نعقل المشار إليه بقوله : ( أنا ) حال ما أكون غافلا عن الجسم

RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r6.claim: Others say the soul is a subtle, luminous celestial body whose attachment animates the body and whose departure leaves it dead.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r6.anchor: بل هو جوهر جسماني لطيف صاف بعيد عن مشابهة الأجرام العنصرية نوراني سماوي

RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r7.claim: On the immaterial view, the soul's return and coming mean managing the body and ceasing that management; on the subtle-body view, they are literal.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r7.anchor: وعلى التقدير الأول يكون وصفها بالمجيء والرجوع بمعنى التدبير وتركه ، وعلى التقدير الثاني يكون ذلك الوصف حقيقا

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r1.speaker: Āl, Q, R, Sy
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r1.claim: The address to the soul at peace is attributed either to angels or directly to God, and occurs at death or Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r1.anchor: It is said that these verses are an address from the angels to human beings

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r2.claim: The verses are prominent in Muslim funeral eulogies; Sufis see them as describing the soul's true nature once purified.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r2.anchor: They play an important role in Muslim piety, as they are often recited in eulogies for the dead

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r3.speaker: Q, Qu, R
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r3.claim: The soul at peace has certainty, like Abraham's heart at peace; it also possesses gnosis and rests in God's remembrance, with degrees of remembrance, certainty, and peace corresponding.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r3.anchor: The soul at peace is said to be the soul that has certainty

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r4.speaker: Jurjānī
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r4.claim: The soul is illuminated by the heart, its blameworthy traits removed and praiseworthy traits made manifest.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r4.anchor: Others speak of the soul so illuminated by the heart that all blameworthy character traits have been removed

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r5.speaker: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r5.claim: Ubayy read the verse as addressing a secure soul at peace, implying immunity from fear and sorrow unlike those in verses 15–16.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r5.anchor: read this verse as “O thou soul secure

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r6.claim: The soul has three levels: the peaceful soul controls desires and has certainty, the blaming soul struggles against desire, and the soul commanding evil is ruled by desire.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r6.anchor: The soul is said to have three levels: the soul at peace (v. 27), which is in command of its lusts and desires

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r7.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r7.claim: A Sufi description presents the peaceful soul as created by primordial divine light, at peace with God and His Address, and oriented solely toward witnessing God.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r7.anchor: Then its Lord calls it to its first origin

SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r1.claim: The common reading uses feminine vocative yā ayyatuhā; Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads masculine yā ayyuhā, a form otherwise rejected except by the author of al-Badīʿ.
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r1.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة " يا أيتها " بتاء التأنيث. وقرأ زيد بن علي " يا أيها " كنداء المذكر

SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r2.claim: The masculine form can be defended because ayyuhā does not agree in number with dual or plural addressees, so it need not agree in gender either.
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r2.anchor: ولم يجوز ذلك أحد، إلا صاحب " البديع " ، وهذه شاهدة له. وله وجه:

SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r3.claim: Rāḍiyatan and marḍiyyatan are two simultaneous circumstantial descriptions; one does not necessarily entail the other.
SAMIN-DURR:89:27/r3.anchor: حالان، أي جامعة بين الوصفين؛ لأنه لا يلزم من أحدهما الآخر.

TAB:89:27/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r1.speaker: author
TAB:89:27/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is one that trusted God's promise to believers in this life of honor in the afterlife and believed it.
TAB:89:27/r1.anchor: التي اطمأنت إلى وعد الله الذي وعد أهل الإيمان به ،   في الدنيا من الكرامة في الاَخرة ،   فصدّقت بذلك .

TAB:89:27/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:27/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls the tranquil soul believing or affirming.
TAB:89:27/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس يا أيّتُها النْفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ يقول :  المصدّقة .

TAB:89:27/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:27/r3.claim: Qatāda says it is the believer whose soul is reassured by God's promise.
TAB:89:27/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ هو المؤمن اطمأنت نفسه إلى ما وعد الله .

TAB:89:27/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r4.speaker: قتادة والحسن
TAB:89:27/r4.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan say it is reassured by God's words and believes what He said.
TAB:89:27/r4.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن ،   في قوله يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ قال :  المطمئنة إلى ما قال الله

TAB:89:27/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:89:27/r5.claim: Mujāhid describes the soul as certain that God is its Lord and resolute in obeying Him; he also calls it humble and at peace with God.
TAB:89:27/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   في قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ قال :  النفس التي أيقنت أن الله ربها

TAB:89:27/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r6.speaker: أبي
TAB:89:27/r6.claim: A recitation attributed to Ubayy adds al-āmina, the secure soul; al-Kalbī explains secure here as believing.
TAB:89:27/r6.anchor: في قراءة أُبيّ :  «يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ الاَمِنَةُ المُطْمِئَنّةُ » وقال الكلبي :  إن الاَمنة في هذا الموضع

TAB:89:27/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r7.speaker: سعيد
TAB:89:27/r7.claim: After the verse was recited before the Prophet and Abū Bakr praised it, the Prophet said the angel would say it to Abū Bakr at death.
TAB:89:27/r7.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «أما إنّ المَلَكَ سَيَقُولُهَا لك عِنْدَ المَوْتِ »

TAB:89:27/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r9.speaker: أبو أسامة بن زيد عن أبيه
TAB:89:27/r9.claim: A report says the tranquil soul is promised the Garden at death, on the Day of Gathering, and at resurrection.
TAB:89:27/r9.anchor: عن أُسامة بن زيد ،   عن أبيه ،   في قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ قال :  بُشّرت بالجنة

TAB-FULL:v24p393/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the reassured soul as one who affirms or believes.
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] يقول: المصدقة

TAB-FULL:v24p393/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies it as the believer whose soul trusts what God has promised.
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] : هو المؤمن اطمأنت نفسه إلى ما وعد الله

TAB-FULL:v24p393/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r3.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan describe the soul as reassured by God's words and affirming them.
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، والحسن، في قوله {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] قال: المطمئنة إلى ما قال الله، والمصدقة بما قال

TAB-FULL:v24p393/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r4.claim: Mujāhid says the soul is certain that God is its Lord and firmly submits to His command and obedience.
TAB-FULL:v24p393/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] قال: النفس التي أيقنت أن الله ربها، وضربت جأشا لأمره وطاعته

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r1.claim: Mujāhid also glosses the reassured soul as humble and submissive to God.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] قال: المخبتة

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r2.claim: Mujāhid describes it as certain of meeting God and steadfast before Him.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] قال: التي أيقنت بلقاء الله، وضربت له جأشا

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r3.speaker: أبيّ
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r3.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy calls the soul secure or safe.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r3.anchor: وذكر أن ذلك في قراءة أبي: «يا أيتها النفس الآمنة»

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī explains āmina here as meaning a believing soul.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: إن الآمنة في هذا الموضع، يعني به المؤمنة

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r8.speaker: أبو أسامة بن زيد عن أبيه
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r8.claim: Usāma b. Zayd reports from his father that the soul receives glad tidings of Paradise at death, the gathering, and the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r8.anchor: عن أسامة بن زيد، عن أبيه، في قوله: {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] قال: بشرت بالجنة عند الموت، ويوم الجمع، وعند البعث

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r9.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r9.claim: Some Kufan grammarians read the reassured soul as faith and affirmation of reward and resurrection, then begin to explain the return as an address to it.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r9.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة يتأول ذلك {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] بالإيمان، والمصدقة بالثواب والبعث ارجعي

ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r1.claim: When calling a woman, one may say yā ayyatuhā or yā ayyuhā; the former treats ayā as feminine, while the latter reflects its ambiguity and construction.
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r1.anchor: " أي " تؤنث إذا دعوت بها مؤنثا وتذكر، تقول: يا أيتها المرأة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r2.claim: Sībawayh reports that some Arabs say kullatuhunna for kulluhunna.
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r2.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن بعض العرب تقول كلتهن في كلهن

ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r3.claim: The tranquil soul is settled in faith and humbly devoted to its Lord.
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r3.anchor: والمطمئنة التي اطمأنت بالإيمان وأخبتت إلى ربها

TABRISI:89:29-30/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r6.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد
TABRISI:89:29-30/r6.claim: The tranquil soul is a believer secure in faith, certain of resurrection and reward.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r6.anchor: بالإيمان المؤمنة الموقنة المصدقة بالثواب والبعث والطمأنينة حقيقة الإيمان

TABRISI:89:29-30/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:89:29-30/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the soul is reassured by news of Paradise at death and on Resurrection Day.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r7.anchor: الآمنة بالبشارة بالجنة عند الموت ويوم البعث عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:89:29-30/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r8.speaker: الكلبي، أبو روق
TABRISI:89:29-30/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī and Abū Rawq describe the tranquil soul as one whose face brightens and whose record is given in the right hand.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r8.anchor: التي يبيض وجهها ويعطى كتابها بيمينها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is assured of God’s reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: بثواب الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r2.claim: The soul has acted with certainty in what God said in His Book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: التي عملت على يقين بما ذكر الله في

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r3.claim: The soul is tranquil through faith.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r4.claim: It is repentant, humble, certain that God is its Lord, resolute in obeying Him, and content with God’s decree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المنيبة المخبتة التي أيقنت بأن الله (ربها) (¬1)، وضربت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r5.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r5.claim: The soul is believing and certain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: المؤمنة الموقنة (¬4). ومعنى هذه الأقوال: المطمئنة إلى وعد الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r6.claim: These interpretations share the sense of a soul assured by God’s promise and affirming what He has said.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r6.anchor: ومعنى هذه الأقوال: المطمئنة إلى وعد الله، المصدقة بما قال.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r7.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r7.claim: Tranquility means certainty, as in Abraham’s request that his heart become tranquil; it is the reality of faith, already established in a believer’s worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p526/r7.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: المطمئنة الموقنة اعتبارا بقوله: {ولكن ليطمئن قلبي}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r3.claim: “Tranquil” can mean safe from punishment, supported by Ubayy’s reading “safe, tranquil soul.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r3.anchor: من العذاب يدل هذا على ما ذكر في حرف أبي:

WAHIDI-QT:89:27/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:27/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:27/r1.claim: The reassured soul believes what God has promised.
WAHIDI-QT:89:27/r1.anchor: { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } إلى ما وعد الله سبحانه المصدقة بذاك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is confident in what God promised and believes it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r1.anchor: إلى ما وعد الله سبحانه المصدقة بذاك

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r1.claim: The address is narrated as a future divine saying, preparing the listener for that day; the believer had already found tranquility through faith, sincerity, and offering good to God.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r1.anchor: Bu üslûb-i ifade Kur’ân’ın i‘câzı tarzlarından birisidir. Bunda sâmi‘i derhâl istikbâle hazırlayacak bir telkin vardır

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r6.claim: Nafs basically means a thing’s own essence; for a person it is the self that says “I” and has unified awareness through different states.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r6.anchor: “nefs” bir şeyin kendisi denilen zât ve hakikatidir

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r7.claim: The self has both perceiving and perceived aspects; in sleep, heedlessness, fainting, or death those aspects may be considered apart, and nafs can name either sentient desire or rational discerning spirit.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r7.anchor: biri duyan, şâ‘ir, biri de duyulan, meş‘ur olmak üzere iki haysiyeti hâizdir

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r8.claim: The self’s unity is grounded in the higher reality of God, who comes between a person and their heart and gathers people to Him.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r8.anchor: insanın nefsine intıbâkı, cihet-i vahdeti kendisinde değil, kendisinin fevkinde bir hakikattedir

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r9.claim: The spirit is from the Lord’s command, and God takes souls at death and during sleep; separation from ordinary awareness is return to God, not annihilation.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r9.anchor: mısdâkınca rûh, emr-i Rab olduğu gibi

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r10.claim: Some commentators take nafs here to mean the self or essence, while others take it to mean the spirit; mutmainna can accordingly describe either.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r10.anchor: Burada çokları zât mânasına bazıları da rûh mânasına telakkī etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r11.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r11.claim: Razi’s first account of tranquility is attaining certainty in the truth that no doubt can disturb, as in Abraham’s request for his heart to be reassured.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r11.anchor: Birincisi, hiçbir şüphe ile bulanmayacak vechile hakka yakīn zevkine ermektir

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r12.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r12.claim: Razi’s second account is security from fear and grief, promised at death, resurrection, and entry into Paradise.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r12.anchor: havf ü hüzünden sarsılmayacak vechile emniyet hâsıl etmektir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r1.claim: The third account of tranquility is that hearts rest only through remembrance of God, as both Qur’an and rational proof establish.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r1.anchor: bu itmi’nân ancak zikrullah ile olur

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r2.claim: Razi’s first rational proof says the intellect keeps seeking a cause beyond every contingent cause until it reaches the Necessary Existent, where it can rest.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r2.anchor: tâ bütün hâcetlerin kesildiği ve bütün zarûretlerin müntehî olduğu vücûdu kendinden, lizâtihî Vâcibü’l-vücûd’a müntehî oluncaya kadar gider

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r3.claim: Razi’s second proof says humans have limitless needs but finite things cannot meet them; tranquility therefore requires God’s limitless perfection.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r3.anchor: abdin nihâyetsiz olan hâceti mukabilinde Allah’ın nihâyetsiz olan kemâli lâzımdır ki istikrar hâsıl olabilsin

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r4.claim: The tranquil soul chooses knowledge of God for God alone and is attached to Him in love, desire, abiding, and speech.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r4.anchor: her kim ma‘rifetullâhı onun gayri bir şey için olmayarak ihtiyar ederse işte o nefs-i mutmainnedir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r5.claim: A tranquil soul is defined by rising through unstable causes to know the First Source, relying only on God, and obeying Him with exclusive sincerity.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r5.anchor: esbâb ve müsebbebât silsilelerinden geçip bizzat müessir olan Mebde’-i A‘lâ’yı mârifete yükselerek

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r6.claim: This definition entails submission to God with excellence, certainty of release from fear and sorrow, and dedicating the self to seek only God’s pleasure.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r6.anchor: Allah için İslâm ve ihsan ile havf u hüzünden

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r7.claim: True freedom means escaping the animal ego, self-reproach, and bondage to anything besides God, then doing every good one can with life and wealth in God’s path.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r7.anchor: nefs-i emmâre tekāzâsından, nefs-i levvâme melâmetinden, mâsivâya esaret kaydlarından kurtarıp

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r8.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the tranquil soul as one that confirms the truth.

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r9.speaker: Katâde
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r9.claim: Qatadah describes it as assured by God’s promise and confirming His word.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r9.anchor: Katâde’den: Allah’ın vaadine mutmain, kavlini musaddık

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r10.speaker: Mücâhid
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r10.claim: Mujahid says it is certain that God is its Lord and submits to His command in every deed.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r10.anchor: Mücâhid’den: Allah, rabbi olduğunu musaddık mûkın ve her yaptığı işte O’nun emrine müslim

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r11.claim: Another formulation says the soul is certain God is its Lord, gives its heart only to Him, and has a heart that beats by His command; it is repentant and humble.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r11.anchor: Allah rabbi olduğuna îkān etmiş, gönlünü ancak O’na vermiş, kalbi O’nun emriyle çarpar

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r12.claim: Reports describing certainty of meeting God and a heart beating with longing for Him also point to the complementary Qur’anic descriptions of believers and the humble.

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r13.claim: Sufi writers discuss the soul’s ranks, stations, and states; Sufism as a whole revolves around the maxim that knowing oneself leads to knowing one’s Lord.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r13.anchor: Hatta bütün tasavvuf مَنْ عَرَفَ نـَفْسَهُ فـَقَدْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r14.claim: Sufis enumerate seven soul-states: commanding, self-reproaching, tranquil, content, accepted, inspired, and purified.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r14.anchor: Nefs-i emmâre, nefs-i levvâme, nefs-i mutmainne, nefs-i râzıye, nefs-i marziyye

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r15.claim: The preceding account contrasts the ignorant, worldly commanding soul and belatedly self-reproaching soul with the tranquil soul that understood truth in time.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r15.anchor: nefs-i emmâre ve nefs-i levvâme hükümleri gösterilmiş, sonra da vaktiyle hakkı anlayıp

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.claim: Exegetes differ on whether this address comes at death, resurrection, or after the reckoning; the author considers the last timing most apparent from the context.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.anchor: Bunda üç kavil vardır: Ölüm zamanında olması, ba‘s zamanında

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r1.speaker: İkrime
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r1.claim: Ikrima and Dahhak report that the address and command to return occur at resurrection; on this reading the soul returns to its Lord for eternal life.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r1.anchor: İkrime ve Dahhâk’ten rivayet olunduğuna göre bu hitab ile ٱرْجِعِىٓ emri ba‘s sırasındadır

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r5.speaker: İbn Cübeyr
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r5.claim: Ibn Jubayr reports that when this verse was recited before Abu Bakr, the Prophet told him an angel would say it to him at death.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r5.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem de أَمَا إِنَّ الْمَلَكَ سَيـَقُولُ لَكَ عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r6.speaker: Hakîm-i Tirmizî
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r6.claim: Hakim al-Tirmidhi transmits a similar report from Abu Bakr through Sulaym ibn Amir.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r6.anchor: b. Aclân tarîkiyle Selim b. Âmir’den, Hazret-i Sıddîk radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet eylemiştir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r7.claim: If the address occurs at death, nafs means spirit and returning is the spirit’s departure from the body toward its Lord.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r7.anchor: Bu surette “nefs” rûh mânasına olup rücû‘u rûhun bedenden iftirâkıyla Rabbine doğru

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.claim: Though Abu Salih’s reading seems apparent, the context favors the address after resurrection and completed reckoning; the reports can fit by treating each death as a person’s resurrection or the commands together as a unit.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.anchor: bu hitâbın da o güne ait olması iktizâ edeceğinden ba‘de’l-ba‘s

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.speaker: Zeyd b. Eslem
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that the tranquil soul is given this address at death, resurrection, and the gathering, and is promised Paradise.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.anchor: mutmainne ölüm sırasında ve ba‘s sırasında ve cem‘günü cennet ile tebşir olunmuştur

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.claim: The majority understand an omitted “God will say” from the preceding context, making the address and commands declarative and creative rather than legislative.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.anchor: cumhûrun muhtârı budur. Buna göre bu hitâbın ve emirlerin teşrî‘î değil tekvînî olması

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.claim: The author also considers a direct, legislative divine address at the surah’s conclusion plausible; separation from what precedes highlights that the tranquil souls themselves should hear it.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.anchor: bunun nüfûs-i mutmainne tarafından re’sen ve bilhassa istimâ‘ı maksud olduğuna tenbih için

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r14.claim: Some exegetes take the address as applying to the tranquil soul in worldly life at all times; the author finds this clearer and more useful.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r14.anchor: bir kısım müfessirîn de bunun nefs-i mutmainneye dünyada da her zaman için hitab olduğuna kāil olmuştur

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.claim: The life of a tranquil soul among the righteous is like the ten nights before Eid al-Adha, and its entry into Paradise is the dawn of the greatest festival of bliss.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.anchor: dünya ömrü îd-i adhâya tekaddüm eden bir leyâl-i aşr

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.claim: The commentator prays that he and his readers return to God content and accepted, join His sincere servants, and reach Paradise and the vision of God.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.anchor: bu abd-i hakīri ve bunları hüsn-i nazarla okuyup ona hayırhah olanları

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r21.claim: The closing supplication asks God for a tranquil soul that believes in meeting Him, accepts His decree, and is content with His gift.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r21.anchor: نـَفْسًا مُطْمَئِنَّةً تـُؤْمِنُ بِلِقَائِكَ وَتـَرْضَى بِقَضَائِكَ

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.claim: Later verses 27–30 add a positive afterlife ending to the earlier threat-only conclusion, pairing entry into the Garden with the Hell mentioned in verse 23.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.claim: All three insertions use direct speech: the human responds to worldly allotment and threatened Hell, then God's address to the trusting soul and servants supersedes those negative statements.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.anchor: Auffällig ist, dass alle drei Einschübe – V. 15.16, V. 23.24 und V. 27–30 – wörtliche Reden enthalten

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r3.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r3.claim: Neuwirth sees the trusting soul as recalling the oath's worship times, which especially embody confidence and inner calm in God's nearness.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r3.anchor: Neuwirth erblickt in V. 27–30 einen motivischen Rückbezug auf die Schwureinleitung

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is the believer who completed earthly life according to the model of revering God's commands and showing compassion to creation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r1.anchor: Allah’ın emrine saygı ve Allah’ın yarattıklarına şefkat

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r2.claim: Nafs mutma'inna denotes a believer whose soul matured through a life lived according to that model.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r2.anchor: “imanın huzuruna kavuşmuş insan”, dünya hayatını bu modele göre yaşayıp tamamlamış olan mümindir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.claim: Addressing the person directly without an introductory afterlife formula is a graceful, warm honor that lets the promise of otherworldly happiness reach into this life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.anchor: doğrudan insana hitap edilmesi, Cenâb-ı Hakk’ın bu yapıdaki kullarına çok güzel bir iltifatı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r4.claim: At this station inner conflict, distress, and tension end; the person is at peace with God, other people, and himself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r4.anchor: Allah ile barışık, insanlarla barışık ve kendisiyle barışıktır

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p372/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p372/r1.speaker: قتادة والحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p372/r1.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan describe the tranquil soul as assured by what God has said and affirming it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p372/r1.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ﴾ قال المطمئنة إلى ما قال الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r1.claim: This passage depicts the state of one at rest through God's remembrance and obedience, contrasted with the person settled in worldly life; God is understood to be speaking, directly or through an angel, likely after judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى يا أيها النفس المطمئنة الخ حكاية لا حوال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r2.claim: One interpretation makes the nafs the self: reason ascends through causes to the First Cause, and the soul becomes calm upon knowing and relying wholly on God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r2.anchor: والنفس قيل بمعنى الذات ووصفت بالاطمئنان بذلك لأنها لترقي بقوتها العاقلة في معارج الأسباب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r3.claim: Another, which al-Alusi calls a good interpretation, is the believer certain of truth, whose heart has no doubt or disturbance; this links remembrance to the strength of certainty and 39:9.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r3.anchor: وقيل هي النفس المؤمنة المطمئنة إلى الحق الواصلة إلى ثلج اليقين وبرودته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r4.claim: A further view is the believer who feels no fear or grief at resurrection; Abu's reading “secure, at rest” supports it and contrasts with the earlier grieving person.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r4.anchor: وقيل هي الأمنة التي لا يستفزها خوف ولا حزن يوم القيامة أعني النفس المؤمنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130/r5.speaker: أبو
